policy: Owner slots and observable exit contracts are assigned now. Except for M06-D, these are planned authoring obligations, not implemented lessons or clearance evidence. Branch prerequisites are AND gates; a later macro title does not clear them. Preserve all 65 macro IDs and order.

extensions.title: Proof-based analysis bridge
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Completeness and subsequences
units.exitTask: Construct a bounded sequence, extract a convergent subsequence using nested intervals, and prove the limiting point exists using real completeness.

units.title: Finite-dimensional compactness
units.exitTask: Prove closed-and-bounded compactness in R^d via coordinate subsequences; prove a finite product of simplexes is nonempty, compact and convex.

units.title: Continuity and extreme values
units.exitTask: Prove continuous images preserve sequential compactness, derive EVT, and refute the claim after removing compactness.

units.title: Open-cover and sequential formulations
units.exitTask: Prove the equivalence needed in finite-dimensional metric spaces; distinguish pointwise closedness from compactness.

extensions.title: Finite expected-utility representation
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Ordinal preferences versus lottery utility
units.exitTask: Construct two monotone transformations of deterministic rankings that disagree on a lottery; identify why only positive affine transformations preserve all expected-utility comparisons.

units.title: Lottery domain and preference axioms
units.exitTask: State completeness/transitivity, mixture continuity and mixture independence on the full simplex over finite consequences; test each axiom on an explicit preference relation.

units.title: Best/worst lotteries and standard gambles
units.exitTask: Using finite best/worst consequences, prove every lottery is indifferent to a standard best/worst mixture; handle the all-indifferent case separately.

units.title: Finite vNM representation
units.exitTask: Prove the standard-gamble index is affine under mixture using independence, then derive U(p)=sum_x p(x)u(x) and prove the converse.

units.title: Positive affine uniqueness
units.exitTask: Prove normalized representations agree using standard gambles; recover u′=a u+b with a>0 in the nontrivial case.

units.title: Axiom failures and model boundaries
units.exitTask: Construct an independence violation, distinguish a supplied utility model from a revealed preference representation, and explain why the finite theorem does not establish utility over every infinite outcome domain.

extensions.title: Limits and legal interchange
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Uniform versus pointwise convergence
units.exitTask: Construct f_n(x)=x^n on [0,1], find its pointwise limit, and show it is not uniform; prove uniform limits preserve continuity.

units.title: Termwise integration
units.exitTask: Prove the bounded-interval uniform-convergence integration rule using a sup-norm bound and give an explicit failure when hypotheses are absent.

units.title: Derivative interchange and series
units.exitTask: Prove a correctly stated differentiation-under-uniform-derivative theorem with an anchor value; justify a power-series operation on compact subintervals of its convergence interval.

units.title: Counterexamples and convergence-test scope
units.exitTask: Build a narrowing spike showing pointwise convergence alone does not justify integral interchange; prove the ratio/comparison tests actually used before claiming them.

extensions.title: Measure and probability foundations
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Measurable spaces and sigma-algebras
units.exitTask: Construct a nontrivial sigma-algebra, classify its measurable functions, and prove closure under countable set operations.

units.title: Probability measures and measurable random variables
units.exitTask: Define countable additivity; derive continuity of measure from below/above with its finite-mass hypotheses and pushforward distributions.

units.title: Lebesgue expectation
units.exitTask: Construct expectation from nonnegative simple functions and monotone approximation; separate signed integrability from an undefined infinity-minus-infinity expression.

units.title: Convergence and integration theorems
units.exitTask: Prove monotone convergence and Fatou, derive dominated convergence with an explicit integrable dominator, and produce a counterexample without it.

units.title: Product laws and iterated integration
units.exitTask: State and apply Tonelli/Fubini with nonnegative/absolute-integrability hypotheses and distinguish a product law from an arbitrary joint law.

units.title: Absolute continuity and Radon–Nikodym existence
units.exitTask: Prove the finite-measure Radon–Nikodym theorem with its absolute-continuity hypotheses, including the Hahn-decomposition/simple-function construction lemmas used; derive a measurable density and prove almost-sure uniqueness.

units.title: Conditional expectation
units.exitTask: Construct finite-partition conditional expectation, then prove the defining integral identity and almost-sure uniqueness; teach the existence theorem with its Radon–Nikodym prerequisite explicitly before general use.

extensions.requiredProofBridge: M26-P-06 owns the finite-measure Radon–Nikodym proof before M26-P-07 general conditional-expectation existence. A theorem left assumed cannot clear the proof-complete probability gate.

extensions.title: Probabilistic convergence and asymptotics
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Modes of convergence
units.exitTask: Define almost-sure, in-probability, in-distribution and Lp convergence; prove valid implication arrows and construct counterexamples to their converses.

units.title: Uniform integrability
units.exitTask: Prove a stated uniform-integrability criterion and the expectation-convergence theorem actually used; distinguish it from pointwise convergence and a uniform bound on first moments.

units.title: Borel–Cantelli and event limits
units.exitTask: Prove both Borel–Cantelli lemmas with the correct summability/independence hypotheses and construct an example showing why the second conclusion can fail without independence.

units.title: Characteristic functions and uniqueness
units.exitTask: Define characteristic functions, prove the uniqueness/inversion tools at the exact scope used, and distinguish a transform identity from an unproved distributional convergence assertion.

units.title: Levy continuity bridge
units.exitTask: Prove the characteristic-function continuity theorem needed for the chosen CLT, including tightness/subsequence arguments and the continuity-at-zero hypothesis.

units.title: Weak law with explicit moment assumptions
units.exitTask: Prove the finite-variance iid weak law from Chebyshev and identify exactly where independence and finite variance enter; avoid claiming this proves every strong law.

units.title: Finite-variance iid central limit theorem
units.exitTask: Derive the characteristic-function expansion from finite variance, prove the iid normalization limit and apply the owned Levy continuity theorem to establish the CLT.

units.title: Conditional expectation calculus
units.exitTask: Prove tower and measurable pull-out identities under integrability assumptions; use them on nested information partitions and then on the general conditional-expectation definition.

extensions.title: Ruin, martingales and stopping
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Finite-state gambler ruin
units.exitTask: Derive hitting probabilities for barriers 0,N by first-step recurrence; handle p=1/2 separately and distinguish finite barriers from a limit as N→∞.

units.title: Filtrations and stopping times
units.exitTask: Construct filtrations and classify stopping rules using information available at time n; exhibit a rule using future information that is not a stopping time.

units.title: Integrable martingales
units.exitTask: Verify a process is adapted, integrable and satisfies E[M_{n+1}|F_n]=M_n; supply a counterexample failing each hypothesis.

units.title: Bounded optional stopping
units.exitTask: For T≤N, write M_T=M_0+sum_{k<N}1_{T>k}(M_{k+1}−M_k), prove measurability and zero expectation of each term, then derive E[M_T]=E[M_0].

units.title: Unbounded stopping and failed extrapolation
units.exitTask: Use a symmetric random walk stopped on first hitting +1 to show almost-sure finite stopping alone does not preserve expectation; prove a chosen UI/bounded-increment-and-integrable-time extension only after its extra hypotheses.

units.title: Infinite-horizon ruin limits
units.exitTask: Derive the one-sided nearest-neighbor ruin law from finite barriers using continuity of probability and distinguish drift cases; do not confuse this with an arbitrary bankroll/control process.

extensions.boundedFiniteEntry: Finite-state/bounded-horizon results may be taught first using M04/M26; general integrable/unbounded statements require advancedRequires.

extensions.title: Brownian foundations, without stochastic calculus
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Consistent Gaussian finite-dimensional laws
units.exitTask: Construct the centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), verify positive semidefiniteness and consistency, and distinguish law specification from process existence.

units.title: Kolmogorov extension and process existence
units.exitTask: State and prove the extension theorem at the Polish/Borel finite-dimensional scope actually used, apply consistency, and identify the coordinate sigma-algebra of the resulting path space.

units.title: Continuous modification
units.exitTask: Prove the required moment/continuity criterion using dyadic control and the owned Borel–Cantelli tools, then derive a continuous Brownian modification from Gaussian increment moments.

units.title: Scaling and increments
units.exitTask: Prove Brownian scaling and independent stationary increments from the Gaussian finite-dimensional laws; distinguish equality in law from pathwise equality.

units.title: Brownian martingales
units.exitTask: Verify the basic Brownian and compensated-square martingale identities under the declared filtration and integrability assumptions, without assuming an Ito formula.

units.title: Grid simulation and its limits
units.exitTask: Construct a reproducible Gaussian-increment grid simulator, check its exact finite-dimensional moments and explain why a finite plot cannot establish path continuity or stochastic calculus.

extensions.title: Game theory: existence, certificates and learning
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Finite normal-form games
units.exitTask: Construct a three-player game, the product of mixed-strategy simplexes, and expected utilities under independent player randomization; distinguish a correlated joint law.

units.title: Best responses and support
units.exitTask: Prove it suffices to check pure deviations and characterize equilibrium support inequalities; verify a degenerate example including unused actions.

units.title: Sperner in arbitrary finite dimension
units.exitTask: State legal boundary labels for a triangulated d-simplex, prove the parity/induction argument for every finite d, and explain why a triangle-only proof does not cover arbitrary games.

units.title: Brouwer fixed-point bridge
units.exitTask: Use vanishing-mesh Sperner subdivisions plus compactness to prove Brouwer for a simplex, then explicitly transfer to the compact convex finite-dimensional strategy domain; reject a discontinuous self-map.

units.title: The continuous Nash map
units.exitTask: Construct F_ia(x)=[x_ia+max(0,u_i(a,x_-i)−u_i(x))]/[1+sum_b max(0,u_i(b,x_-i)−u_i(x))]; prove continuity, simplex preservation and a positive denominator.

units.title: General finite Nash existence
units.exitTask: At a fixed point put g_ia=max(0,u_i(a,x_-i)−u_i(x)) and G_i=sum g_ia. Prove x_ia G_i=g_ia and use sum_a x_ia[u_i(a,x_-i)−u_i(x)]=0 to rule out G_i>0; apply Brouwer to prove a mixed Nash equilibrium exists for any finite number of players/actions.

units.title: What existence does not imply
units.exitTask: Construct a game with no pure equilibrium and one with several equilibria; distinguish existence, uniqueness, efficiency and dynamic convergence.

units.title: Zero-sum games as linear programs
units.exitTask: Derive row primal max v subject to Aᵀx≥v1, x≥0, 1ᵀx=1, and column dual min w subject to Ay≤w1, y≥0, 1ᵀy=1; establish feasibility and boundedness.

units.title: Finite minimax via strong duality
units.exitTask: Use the proven M53 LP strong-duality theorem to derive max_x min_y xᵀAy=min_y max_x xᵀAy for every finite rectangular matrix, including negative payoffs and degenerate optima.

units.title: Saddle and complementary-slackness certificates
units.exitTask: Construct primal/dual policies and matching bounds for a rectangular game; prove support indifference and inequalities for unused actions instead of relying on equalizing all entries.

units.title: Correlated-equilibrium constraints
units.exitTask: Construct a mediator joint distribution and derive every obedience inequality; distinguish correlation from independent mixed play.

units.title: Correlated-equilibrium existence
units.exitTask: Convert an existing mixed Nash profile to its product joint law and verify all obedience constraints; explain why CE existence does not require a unique Nash solution.

units.title: Regret and empirical distributions
units.exitTask: Derive that vanishing external regret yields coarse-correlated equilibrium of empirical play; demonstrate why ordinary external regret alone does not prove correlated equilibrium or last-iterate Nash convergence.

units.title: Existence versus computation
units.exitTask: Measure unilateral-deviation residuals of candidate solutions and give an epsilon-equilibrium certificate; separate a numerical fixed-point iteration from a proof that it converges.

units.title: Kakutani bridge for compact games
units.exitTask: Define upper hemicontinuity, nonempty compact convex values and closed graphs; teach/prove the finite-dimensional Kakutani theorem used, rather than cite an unowned theorem.

units.title: Compact-action pure equilibrium existence
units.exitTask: For compact convex strategy sets, continuous payoffs quasiconcave in each player’s own strategy, prove the best-response correspondence satisfies Kakutani hypotheses and derive equilibrium; show the role of each hypothesis.

units.title: Infinite-game boundaries
units.exitTask: Construct a discontinuous or noncompact game with no equilibrium and reject unconditional existence claims; do not generalize finite Nash to arbitrary action spaces.

units.title: Game design and independent defence
units.exitTask: Design a finite strategic interaction, state utility/information assumptions, compute or certify equilibria, perturb payoffs and defend whether equilibrium selection or learning claims follow.

subgates.finiteNash: Units01–07; full finite-dimensional fixed-point proof is mandatory.
subgates.minimax: Units08–10 after proven LP strong duality, not merely weak duality or KKT heuristics.
subgates.compactGames: Units15–17 after Kakutani; finite Nash does not certify this subgate.
subgates.laterGames: Repeated-game folk theorems, Bayesian equilibrium, auctions/mechanism design and stochastic games remain separate future specialisations, not implied by these 18 units.

extensions.title: School/entrance algebra, geometry and complex numbers
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Geometry/mensuration diagnostic
units.exitTask: Solve unfamiliar Euclidean similarity, circle and area/volume problems; route missing school geometry to taught remediation.

units.title: Polynomial and Vieta tools
units.exitTask: Derive Vieta/remainder/division tools with legal domains and solve a parameterized polynomial problem.

units.title: Complex/trigonometric entrance bridge
units.exitTask: Teach complex arithmetic and polar form, derive De Moivre and use it in an original roots/geometry task; do not invoke complex analysis.

units.title: Conics and inequalities
units.exitTask: Derive conic equations and solve rational/polynomial sign problems with all domain restrictions.

extensions.title: Entrance counting extension
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Multinomial coefficients
units.exitTask: Derive the multinomial theorem by labelled finite allocation and solve a constrained occupancy task.

extensions.title: Order statistics
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Order-statistic laws
units.exitTask: Derive minimum/maximum/order-statistic laws under an explicitly iid continuous model; treat ties/discrete models separately.

extensions.title: Sufficiency and estimation theory
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Sufficiency and factorization
units.exitTask: Define sufficiency and prove/apply a correctly dominated factorization theorem; do not treat a good estimator as automatically sufficient.

units.title: Rao–Blackwell and completeness scope
units.exitTask: Prove a scoped Rao–Blackwell result using conditional expectation, and distinguish completeness and sufficiency from consistency.

extensions.title: ANOVA and design analyses
extensions.placement: After the owner core; complete all named branch prerequisites before entering.

units.title: Balanced fixed-effects ANOVA
units.exitTask: Derive sums-of-squares decomposition, degrees of freedom and a correctly assumed F comparison for a balanced design.

units.title: Design and interaction
units.exitTask: Construct a randomized block/factorial analysis with interactions and demonstrate confounding; do not extrapolate a one-way ANOVA to all designs.

extensions.title: Finite LP proof bridge for game minimax
extensions.placement: After the M53 optimization core; before M53-G minimax units.

units.title: Primal and dual construction
units.exitTask: Derive a dual linear program with all sign/free-variable conventions and weak-duality certificates; classify infeasible or unbounded cases without assuming strong duality.

units.title: Farkas alternative from finite convex geometry
units.exitTask: Prove closedness of the relevant finitely generated cone and derive Farkas using an explicit separating/projection argument; verify every alternative hypothesis.

units.title: Finite LP strong duality and attainment
units.exitTask: Use the proved alternative to establish primal/dual optimal-value equality and attainment under correctly stated finite LP feasibility/boundedness assumptions, including degeneracy.

units.title: Complementary slackness certificates
units.exitTask: Derive complementary slackness and verify exact primal/dual optimal solutions with zero coordinates and inactive constraints; reject a certificate that only checks stationarity.

extensions.title: Bayesian parameter inference and continuous prediction
extensions.placement: After likelihood and distribution/integration foundations; finite hypothesis prediction is already owned by M06-S34.

units.title: Posterior densities and support
units.exitTask: Construct a continuous posterior from an explicit prior density and sampling law, prove its normalizing integral is positive and finite, and diagnose an improper or support-incompatible posterior.

units.title: Beta-Bernoulli and conjugacy
units.exitTask: Derive the Beta-Bernoulli posterior and normalizer from the likelihood and prior kernel, verify all shape/support conditions, and distinguish finite-hypothesis weights from a continuous parameter density.

units.title: Posterior predictive laws
units.exitTask: Integrate the sampling law over the continuous parameter posterior, derive a predictive probability and explain uncertainty omitted by a point-estimate plug-in.

units.title: Loss-dependent estimates and credible sets
units.exitTask: Derive posterior expected-loss actions under stated squared/absolute/finite-action losses; construct a credible set and explain why its probability statement differs from confidence-interval coverage.

units.title: Prior/model criticism and computation
units.exitTask: Compare priors on an explicit scientific model, check prior and posterior predictive implications with reproducible quadrature or simulation, and refuse a claim that internal Bayes consistency validates the population model.

units.title: Reproducible Bayesian defence
units.exitTask: Defend a small Bayesian analysis with data provenance, identifiability/support checks, prior sensitivity, predictive checks and a held-out evaluation; separate supplied numerical assistance from independent mathematical and coding evidence.
